nodes.label: Conversation Map
nodes.notes: An overview map of what the current conversation is about, not a transcript and not a flat dump of every idea.

nodes.label: Overview concepts
nodes.notes: Large, human-scale clusters shown first so the map stays readable.

nodes.label: Dive-in views
nodes.notes: A selected overview concept opens a focused subgraph or detail panel with more nodes, edges, notes, evidence, and questions.

nodes.label: Capture policy
nodes.notes: The user can choose explicit approval, delegated capture, or another capture rule for the current conversation.

nodes.label: Agent interpretation
nodes.notes: The AI turns approved or delegated conversation signal into graph changes instead of exposing manual editing as the primary workflow.

nodes.label: Semantic graph SSOT
nodes.notes: The graph model remains the source of truth; visual grouping and layout are projections over it.

nodes.label: Detail graph
nodes.notes: The deeper graph behind one overview concept, useful when the human asks to inspect a topic.

nodes.label: Human feedback
nodes.notes: Drag, mark, select, and comment gestures tell the agent what the human meant.

nodes.label: Flat-map overload
nodes.notes: Too many peer-level nodes makes the map visually noisy and reduces usefulness.

nodes.label: Saved demo snapshots
nodes.notes: Earlier POC maps are preserved under data/snapshots for tomorrow's demo.

nodes.label: Category overlay
nodes.notes: A visual/semantic layer that marks whether something is confirmed, inferred, risky, unknown, experimental, stale, mandatory, or custom.

nodes.label: Trust state
nodes.notes: Categories tell humans whether a concept is approved truth, AI inference, critique, unknown, or proven learning.

nodes.label: Project Map
nodes.notes: The same mapping model can represent a project, where categories become more important for decisions, risks, rules, dependencies, and stale architecture.

nodes.label: Custom categories
nodes.notes: Projects can define their own labels such as Microservice, That Idiot, or Vacation plans without changing the core graph model.
